hook: The Pacific Ocean hit a record-breaking 29.7 degrees Celsius in September.

sections.voiceover: The Pacific Ocean hit a record-breaking 29.7 degrees Celsius in September.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite thermal map of the Pacific Ocean with heat intensity shown.
sections.sfx_cue: Low frequency hum of ocean currents.
b_roll: Satellite thermal map of the Pacific Ocean

sections.voiceover: Copernicus Climate Change Service sensors recorded this peak as temperatures across the region surged. But how intense is this Pacific Ocean warming trend during the current 2026 climate cycle?
sections.visual_cue: Data visualization showing temperature rise over the Pacific basin.
b_roll: Scientific data visualization of Pacific surface temperatures

sections.voiceover: Australia's Bureau of Meteorology reports the Niño 3.4 index, tracking central Pacific surface heat, hit +2.81°C.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a meteorological index chart showing the spike.
b_roll: Weather chart showing the Niño 3.4 index spike

sections.voiceover: This +2.81°C surge occurred weeks ahead of the typical December peak for the central Pacific. Tropical Pacific temperatures are climbing toward record levels during this October through December period.
sections.visual_cue: Animation of global temperature trends centered on the Pacific.
b_roll: World Meteorological Organization headquarters in Geneva

sections.voiceover: October through December will likely see these temperatures rise further.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the vast, calm Pacific Ocean at dusk.
b_roll: Wide shot of the Pacific Ocean
